claim: web_fetch SSRF protection can be bypassed via DNS-resolved private/loopback hostnames or HTTP redirects because _validate_web_url never resolves DNS and fetch_webpage_markdown follows redirects without re-validating targets.
evidence: Agent-Core/agent_core/tools/local.py:58-81 _validate_web_url only rejects literal strings in ('localhost','127.0.0.1','::1','0.0.0.0') or literal private/loopback/link-local IP addresses (silently passing any hostname via except ValueError: pass at lines 78-79). Lines 99-106 then execute httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True, max_redirects=5).get(validated_url) without re-running _validate_web_url on redirect Location hops or pinning resolved IPs. Because web_fetch is in EXPLICIT_SAFE_TOOLS (guardrails.py:26), it executes without human approval.
runtimeTrigger: A prompt-injected webpage or user task instructs the agent to call web_fetch on either (1) a hostname resolving to a loopback/link-local IP (such as a DNS alias for 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, or an internal service hostname) or (2) a public URL that responds with HTTP 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:8100/health or http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/. _validate_web_url passes and httpx fetches and returns the internal response body to the agent.

claim: local_isolated sandbox mode executes bash_exec directly on the host OS using only a 4-regex denylist, allowing trivial sandbox escape to read or overwrite host secrets (auth.json, encrypted vaults, .env) and application code.
evidence: When Docker is unavailable (the default SANDBOX_BACKEND=auto fallback), Agent-Core/agent_core/sandbox.py:471-516 _exec_local_isolated checks only the 4 static patterns in _LOCAL_ESCAPE_PATTERNS (lines 44-49: docker.sock, /etc/shadow|passwd|sudoers, /proc/<pid>/environ|mem|root, literal .env) and then spawns bash -c directly on the host filesystem with cwd=workspace_dir and no filesystem namespace, chroot, or mount isolation. Paths such as ../data/auth.json (which stores sessionSecret and vaultMasterSecret), ../data/vaults/*.vault.json, ../data/llm_config.json, and obfuscated reads of ../.env are unrestricted.
runtimeTrigger: On any deployment running in local_isolated mode, an agent tool call to bash_exec (classified SAFE by guardrails.py) reads ../data/auth.json or ../data/vaults/admin.vault.json via standard shell or Python file I/O (or modifies ../server.ts), completely bypassing workspace confinement and exposing the vault master secret and session signing secret.

claim: MCPServerConfig and load_mcp_tools_from_configs connect to caller-supplied MCP server URLs without URL scheme validation or private/metadata network restrictions (SSRF).
evidence: MCPs/manager.py:28-33 defines MCPServerConfig.url as an unvalidated string, and lines 79-97 pass srv.url and arbitrary headers directly to MultiServerMCPClient for streamable_http/sse connections without verifying http(s) scheme or blocking loopback, private RFC1918, or cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) addresses. Agent-Core/agent_core/api.py:575-588 and 745 accept per-request mcp_servers straight into load_mcp_tools_from_configs.
runtimeTrigger: An authenticated caller configures an MCP server via PUT /api/mcps or passes per-request mcp_servers to Agent-Core with url pointing to an internal host or cloud metadata service; Agent-Core initiates outbound HTTP/SSE requests to that internal target and returns connection diagnostics in warnings.

claim: Isolated sub-agent graphs are compiled without a checkpointer while still propagating LangGraph GraphInterrupt, causing HITL approval resume to restart the sub-agent from scratch instead of resuming at the paused tool call.
evidence: Agent-Core/agent_core/subagents.py:473 compiles worker_graph = builder.compile() with no checkpointer. Inside worker_act (lines 428-435), execute_tool_with_guardrails calls langgraph.types.interrupt() for SENSITIVE tools and re-raises GraphInterrupt (lines 434, 507) out of spawn_subagent into the parent act_node. When the parent graph resumes with Command(resume=...), LangGraph re-invokes spawn_subagent -> run_isolated_subagent from initial_worker_state (turn_count=0), re-running all earlier worker LLM calls and side-effecting worker tools and risking non-deterministic divergence before reaching the interrupt.
runtimeTrigger: The supervisor delegates a multi-step task via spawn_subagent; on turn 2 the worker calls a SENSITIVE tool (e.g., bash_exec with rm or an external MCP mutation), pausing the graph for HITL approval. After the user approves, the parent resumes act_node, which restarts worker_graph from turn 0, re-executing turn 1's LLM call and tool calls rather than resuming turn 2.
